newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile arrests fugitive German's alleged impersonator.
newsitem.headline: Chile arrests fugitive German's alleged impersonator.

text.p: Chilean police on Wednesday arrested a man they think impersonated the fugitive leader of a secretive German enclave last weekend in an effort to throw police off his trail, officials said.

German citizen Max Rudolf was nabbed by police during a raid on the Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony) settlement on Wednesday and will be charged with obstruction of justice, Interior Minister Carlos Figueroa said.

Authorities believe Rudolf was the man who checked into a hotel in the Argentine ski resort of Bariloche over the weekend and signed his name in the hotel register as Paul Schaefer, the German immigrant founder of Colonia Dignidad who is wanted on charges of molesting boys.

An anonymous phone call led police to his hotel room but they found only his pajamas and an open window, suggesting he had fled. The incident suggested Schaefer had skipped over the Andes to Argentina, but authorities in Santiago quickly ridiculed the "sighting" as an obvious red herring.
"We think this is the person who supplanted Paul Schaefer," Figueroa told a news conference on Wednesday.
He said border control records showed Rudolf entered and left Chile on roughly the same dates as the Schaefer impostor was in Bariloche and he resembled descriptions of the mysterious hotel guest.

More than 200 police raided the secretive colony on Wednesday seeking to arrest Schaefer. It was the boldest police action yet against the 36-year-old colony, once protected by Chile's military rulers, where settlers came from Germany in the early 1960s to live in secrecy.

Schaefer, a corporal in the Nazi army in the Second World War and now in his late 70s, was believed to be holed up somewhere in the colony although settlers say they have not seen him for about eight months. Officials vowed to find him.
